title: Snowboarding and skiing: from first lesson to pro
intro: Start with your first lessons and Snowsport England Level 1, then pick a track. The UK slope track (Snowsport England) keeps you teaching on UK slopes. The mountain track (BASI) takes you to the top international awards. Both end with coaching, competitions and safety.

sections.title: Start here
sections.intro: Both tracks start with these two steps.

items.summary: Your first lessons in snowboarding and skiing in the UK.
Snowsport England Level 1 (ski or snowboard): teach beginners on UK slopes.

sections.title: UK slope track (Snowsport England)
sections.intro: After Level 2, skiers go on to Ski Development Coach. Snowboarders go to the coaching pathways (step 9).

items.summary: Snowsport England Level 2: teach on your own, with 20 logged hours.
Ski Development Coach, Levels 3 and 4 (ski only).
BASI Level 1: the four-day entry course for ski or snowboard.
BASI Level 2: eight days on the mountain, or the four-day UK Level 2.
BASI Level 3 ISIA: modules, 200 logged hours and a second discipline.
BASI Level 4 ISTD: Teaching, Technical and, for skiers, Freeride.
Coaching pathways: alpine race, park and pipe, moguls and nordic, plus licensing.
Competitions: the English Slopestyle and Alpine Championships, the Scottish Park + Pipe Series and the talent pathway.
Prices, who governs what in England, Scotland and Wales, and the FIS slope code.
